item.title: The US will see a rare 'blood moon' eclipse before sunrise this March: Where and when to look
item.description: A rare total lunar eclipse will be visible from most of the United States on March 3. Here's where and when to look.

item.title: Saltwater crocodiles crossed the Indian Ocean to reach the Seychelles — before humans arrived and wiped them out
item.description: DNA study reveals crocs that lived in the Seychelles represented the westernmost population of saltwater crocodiles, having swam at least 1,800 miles to reach the island.

item.title: Amazfit Active Max review: The best budget smartwatch of 2026?
item.description: The Amazfit Active Max has surprisingly good specs and an unusually wide range of features for a smartwatch that costs just $169.99.

item.title: How well can AI and humans work together? Scientists are turning to Dungeons & Dragons to find out
item.description: D&D is being used as a benchmark to see how well models can make long-term plans, adhere to rules and strategize with a team.

item.title: 7,500-year-old deer skull headdress discovered in Germany indicates hunter-gatherers shared sacred items and ideas with region's first farmers
item.description: The discovery of a deer skull headdress and tools made from antlers at the site of a New Stone Age farming village suggests that hunter-gathers were sharing ideas with the newcomers.

item.title: Martian meteorite that fell to Earth is full of ancient water, new scans reveal
item.description: A new study has revealed that the iconic Black Beauty meteorite contains much more hidden water than previously suspected. The rock, which fell to Earth from Mars, could reveal clues about the Red Planet's watery past.

item.title: Star-killing black hole is one of the most energetic objects in the universe — and it's getting brighter
item.description: Scientists say a jet from a previously studied supermassive black hole has grown brighter, becoming one of the most energetic events in the universe.

item.title: Kanzi the bonobo could play pretend — a trait thought unique to humans
item.description: Past anecdotal observations have hinted that great apes play pretend. But now, experimental research shows that our closest living relatives can keep track of imaginary objects.

item.title: Spotted lanternflies are invading the US. They may have gotten their evolutionary superpowers in China's cities.
item.description: The alarming spread of spotted lanternflies across the U.S. has been made possible by cities acting as evolutionary incubators, fine-tuning the insects and enabling them to thrive.

item.title: The 'mono' virus raises the risk of MS and cancer in some. 22 genes hint at why.
item.description: An infection with Epstein-Barr virus is a nonevent for most people. But for a subset, the virus can contribute to chronic conditions and cancer, and genes may play a role in that risk.
